- When sentiment turns positive (≥0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent high for 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.25) and prices are falling, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model consistently overpredicts in early 30-day horizon (especially 1–7 days ahead); apply 1–3% downward bias for first 7 days.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price range is tight, model tends to average or lag; use 1–2% upward bias for 3–5 days to capture mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often fails to capture momentum; extend upward bias by 0.5–1.0% for 5–7 days.  
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–2% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- If sentiment is positive but price is flat or declining, model overreacts; apply 0.5–1.5% downward correction to avoid false peaks.
